prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first: do you want general advice on how to choose a lawyer, or would you like a short list of specific Pleasanton / Alameda County attorneys to contact? If the latter, tell me any preferences (big firm vs. solo, seriousness of injuries, whether you want a free consult now).

Meanwhile, here’s a practical guide you can use right away.

Key things to look for in a car‑accident/injury lawyer
- Substantial experience handling auto-accident personal injury cases (not just general practice).  
- Contingency-fee arrangement (no fee unless you recover). Typical ranges in CA are roughly 33%–40%, but get fee details in writing.  
- Proven results: settlements/verdicts in similar fact patterns and injuries.  
- Trial/appeal experience if the other side won’t settle.  
- Resources to hire medical experts, accident reconstructionists, etc.  
- Good communication: clear point of contact, timely updates.  
- Local knowledge of Alameda County courts, judges, and insurance companies.  
- Clean disciplinary record (check the CA State Bar website).

Questions to ask at the first (usually free) consult
- How many car-accident injury cases have you handled? How similar is mine?  
- What percentage settle vs go to trial?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (attorney vs paralegal)  
- How do you charge? (contingency percentage, who advances costs, how are costs repaid)  
- What’s your estimate of my case’s value and likely timeline?  
- What documents or evidence will you need?  
- Can you provide client references or recent case results?  
- Any potential conflicts of interest?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report (or report number), photos/video of crash and injuries, vehicle damage photos  
- Medical records, hospital/ER records, medical bills, prescriptions  
- Insurance cards (yours and the other driver’s), claim numbers, any letters/offers from insurers  
- Witness names/contact info, timeline of events, repair estimates, pay stubs (if lost wages)  
- Any text/electronic communications about the crash

Immediate steps to protect your case
- Get prompt medical care and follow treatment recommendations. Document everything.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, vehicle, clothing, dashcam footage.  
- Don’t post details about the crash on social media.  
- Notify your insurer per your policy, but don’t give recorded statements or sign releases without advice.  
- Keep a written log of symptoms, treatment, and missed work.

Red flags when choosing a lawyer
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or to accept the first offer the insurer makes.  
- No written fee agreement or unclear billing for costs.  
- Poor communication or long response delays during the consult process.

Practical ways to find attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.  
- CA State Bar’s “Find a Lawyer” and disciplinary records.  
- Reviews on Google, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, and client testimonials.  
- Ask friends/family or other attorneys (e.g., your family lawyer) for referrals.

Deadlines
- In California the general deadline for personal injury lawsuits is two years from the injury date. Don’t delay contacting a lawyer — evidence and witness memories degrade, and legal deadlines apply.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 Pleasanton/Alameda County personal injury attorneys for you to call (I can include website, phone, and one-line specialties).  
- Draft a short script of what to say and ask during the first call/consult.

Which would you prefer? If you want attorney names, tell me: how serious are your injuries (minor, needing ongoing treatment, hospitalized), and any other preferences.
